newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine launches production of 2 new Antonov jets.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine launches production of 2 new Antonov jets.

text.p: Ukraine's Antonov plane-maker has launched production of two new jets, signalling further recovery in the former Soviet republic's aviation industry, the DINAU-Ukrinform state news agency said on Thursday.
"We already have orders for both types of planes," it quoted Anatoly Myalytsya, director of the eastern Ukrainian plant producing the planes, as saying.
DINAU said one jet, the Antonov-72P, was designed for naval patrolling in any weather, by day or night.
The second jet, a middle-range An-74, could carry 10 tonnes over 4,000 kms (2,500 miles), taking off and landing on short clay runways used in remote parts of Russia and Central Asia.
Local media quoted Yuri Manmar, commander of naval border guards as saying contracts had been signed to buy 10 An-72Ps.
DINAI said two planes would be delivered to Ukrainian border guards and another two to Russian border guards this year.
The planes are to be produced in the eastern industrial city of Kharkiv on the Russian border, and parts would come from Ukraine and Russia under a joint "URAN" consortium.
The same plant can produce up to 40 An-74s annually and dozens of An-72Ps, Hrihory Malyuk, deputy head of Kharkiv adminstration responsible for the economy, told Reuters.
Contracts have already been signed for supplies of 12 An-74 to countries outside the former Soviet Union, the agency added, without specifying where exactly.
Ukraine has been struggling to rejuvenate its Soviet-era aviation industry since it won independence from Moscow in 1991 as domestic carriers rush to lease or buy Western-made jets.

In a bid to turn the tide, the Antonov design bureau has unveiled a series of new models, including a light passenger plane -- the An-38 -- which has passed test flights and can carry 27 passengers or 2.5 tonnes of cargo.
In December, a second model of a cargo An-70 plane was built, and Kiev is hoping it will do well on the international market. It can carry 35 tonnes for 3,500 km (2,200 miles) without refuelling.
The first prototype of a short-haul turbo-prop An-140 is due to be completed next month and test flights are expected in the next few months, an Antonov official told Reuters on Thursday.
The An-140, which carries 52 passengers and 4.9 tonnes of cargo, would replace An-24s, which are widely used in Latin America, Asia and Africa as well as in the former Soviet Union.
